title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P,Q0) for the supplied P; if z=1 output infinity; else solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers shared by all walks, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, deterministic fruitless-cycle escape, a stuck-walk restart after 40/theta steps, a hard global cap of L_max=2^125.6992 counted steps and a hard cap of 2^67 distinguished reports; output Q=[x]Q0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.40 using at most 2^125.89 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts and restarts, distinguished-point handling, candidate solves, cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. Peak memory is below 2^74 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for R-adding rho walks (with the Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction and 3% explicit step slack), supported by toy-field experiments; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, consistency of the canonical representative, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p)=12. Part B: run the complete Frobenius-class rho walk (kappa trick, twisted table, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes, stuck-walk restart after 40/theta steps, distinguished points, collision solving) in a small field with the same tower shape and report collision times against the random-mapping model. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs and does not apply the production caps.
